surfaces.part: top log row with snow patches

answer.evidence: The pile is stacked tiers of log segments. Each tier is a 4-row brown face (rows 13-16, 19-22, 25-28) bounded by 1-row dark lines, as the column scans show. No tier has an edge line followed by eave shadow, no ellipse, and no visible contents. The snow patches at rows 7-10 are small irregular white spots on the log tops, not a horizontal surface band. The whole drawing is vertical faces with outlines, so it is a front elevation. The kind (scattered floor debris) fits poorly, because this is an orderly stack framed by two posts.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a stacked log pile with snow tufts on top. It shows 11 visible tones per 16x16 tile, above prop-hedge (9) and below the stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. The log rows carry rounded ends and alternating warm and dark browns, and the snow caps are speckled rather than one flat white. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines lean dark brown beside the wood, not black, which fits the Beodeul approach. The wood ramp reads as about 4-5 steps against about 5 on the references. The piece is slightly simpler than the stall and well, but it is at least as rich as the hedge reference and not sticker-like.
